bullets.title: August NFP +162k smashes 55k consensus; labor market stronger but not overheating
bullets.body: August nonfarm payrolls printed +162k vs. +55k consensus (+127k private vs. +50k est.), with prior two months revised up a net +55k; 3-month average now +71k. Unemployment held at 4.1%, participation bounced to 61.6%, and wage growth came in soft at +0.3% MoM / +3.1% YoY — well below Fed's 3.5-4.0% target. Multiple banks (MS, Wolfe) conclude data does not change Fed hold outlook; inflation, not labor, remains the policy driver.

bullets.title: Fed on hold: Waller sets high bar for September hike (>0.3% core PCE needed)
bullets.body: September hike odds fell from 70% to 54% after Fed Governor Waller signaled he would hold if core PCE comes in at 0.3% MoM. 10-year yields remain elevated driven by structural cycle dynamics — deficits, AI debt, 6%+ nominal GDP — not Fed policy. Financial conditions have tightened since mid-August, favoring Low Volatility, Quality, and Value factors while pressuring Growth and Momentum.

bullets.title: NFP composition bearish for white-collar: Tech lost 23k jobs, finance -11k, construction +22k
bullets.body: Despite the headline beat, Info Tech shed 23k jobs in August (-115k YoY) and Financial Services back-office fell 11k (-99k YoY), while construction (+22k), manufacturing (+16k), and leisure/hospitality drove all gains. One analyst flags a 'digging our own graves' pattern — economy adding operational/hands-on jobs while higher-paid, digitally-oriented roles shrink — and raises contrarian case for buying Treasuries on yield weakness.

bullets.title: ECB second consecutive hike locked in; energy shock pushes December hike probability higher
bullets.body: WTI/Brent above $90/bbl and European LNG above €70/MWh have pushed euro area HICP to 3.3% in August; TTF gas is 50%+ above the ECB's June forecast assumption of €45.6/MW. ECB is almost certain to hike 25bp to 2.5% next week with hawkish staff forecasts validating ~4 total hikes; a third hike in December is increasingly likely if the Iran-US standoff persists.

bullets.title: OpenAI Astra (GPT-6) deemed AGI moment; trains on 100k GPUs, cuts task costs 50%+
bullets.body: OpenAI released Astra scoring 99.9 on ARC-AGI-3 (vs. Opus at 30.2%) and reducing coding-task costs by more than 50%; US model release cadence accelerated to 12.5 models/quarter in Q3 2026 vs. 7.4 in Q2, a key driver in NVDA datacenter revenue estimation models. OpenAI CTO confirms continued reliance on Nvidia for cutting-edge training despite parallel custom silicon development; NVDA also considering a ~$2.5B investment in Thinking Machines Lab.

bullets.title: MAG7 tests ATHs; NVDA/AAPL lead, software outperforms semis as AI monetization debate intensifies
bullets.body: MAG7 index rose +2.4% on the session with NVDA testing all-time highs alongside AAPL; the GS AI Software Long vs. Semis Short basket is up 18% over the last month (+5.1% yesterday) while the High Beta Momentum factor (Long Semis, Short Software) is down 77% since June. The central GS Communacopia debate: whether $375B+ cumulative AI capex (YE25-YE28) translates to sustainable software/cloud revenue outside frontier hyperscalers.

bullets.title: AI data center demand secular: Citi forecasts 25% IT Load CAGR to 370 GW by 2031
bullets.body: Citi's refreshed data center model projects IT load growing from 121 GW in 2026 to 370 GW in 2031 at a 25% CAGR, driven by AI/HPC workloads and agentic AI adoption; reiterates Buy on EQIX and DLR noting every 100bps upside to 5-year CAGR is ~5% net accretive. Separately, Anthropic is scaling from 2 GW compute capacity in early 2026 to 30 GW by decade-end, with Broadcom XPUs ramping to 70%+ fleet composition and NVDA peaking at ~30% in 2027.

bullets.title: HBM pricing strong but moderating from peak; HBM4 ASP premium >50%, Rubin ramp key H2 catalyst
bullets.body: Korean customs data shows July HBM export value per unit +228% YoY and +10% MoM — healthy but below peak growth rates. HBM4 expected to command >50% ASP premium on a capacity basis over HBM3E, with HBM4E adding another 25-40% premium. The NVDA Rubin platform and custom ASIC ramp in H2 2026 are the primary HBM4 volume drivers.

bullets.title: EDA stocks SNPS -7%, CDNS -5% on OpenAI GPT-6 Astra PCB layout demo despite SOXX +3%
bullets.body: OpenAI released video of GPT-6 Astra performing PCB layout design in KiCad — a historically manual task and key source of latency in electronics design — driving SNPS down 7% and CDNS down 5% while the broader SOXX gained 3%. Market reaction signals investor concern about AI automation risk to EDA software vendors' workflow bottleneck value proposition.

bullets.title: NFLX raises EU prices; AAPL iPhone 18 Pro to start at $1,249-$1,299 on 400% memory cost surge
bullets.body: Netflix raised UK and German prices (AVOD +£2/€1, Standard +£1/€2, Premium +£2/€2), affecting ~18% of EMEA subs and implying ~4% EMEA ARPU uplift. iPhone 18 Pro is expected to start at $1,249-$1,299, up $150-200, driven by 400% YoY increase in 256GB memory costs; supply chain checks suggest 7-8M foldable builds for C2H'26 at a $2,399 starting price.

bullets.title: FHFA mandates VantageScore immediately; FICO -12%, EFX -10% premarket, TRU +12%
bullets.body: FHFA Director Pulte instructed Freddie Mac and Fannie Mae to approve all lenders to use VantageScore immediately, ending a phased rollout and threatening FICO's near-monopoly (up 1,800% in price since 2020). EFX fell ~10% and FICO ~12% in premarket while TRU rose ~12%; UBS maintains EFX Buy at $220 PT citing ~90% proprietary data and ~40% revenue from Workforce Solutions as differentiation.

bullets.title: VIX 14.17 (+1.1%), S&P 7,707 (+0.5%); factor rotation to Quality/Low-Vol from Growth/Momentum
bullets.body: VIX ticked up 1.1% to 14.17 even as S&P 500 gained 0.5% to 7,707.51; options flow shows put-skewed activity across multiple names suggesting elevated hedging demand. Financial conditions tightening since mid-August are driving factor rotation — Quality, Low Volatility, and Value outperforming while Growth and Momentum face headwinds; factor-based long-short portfolio returned 16.8% YTD.

bullets.title: UK inflation expectations inflecting higher; BoE watching wage growth ahead of 2027 pay rounds
bullets.body: DMP survey shows UK 1-year and 3-year CPI inflation expectations rose to 3.1% and 2.7% respectively — first increases since spring — as August PMI input prices jumped 1.1pt to 66.8 and UK natural gas prices have risen 5.8% since survey close. Year-ahead expected wage growth rose to 3.4% from 3.3%, still just below BoE's 3.5% pay settlement estimate; Q3 GDP is tracking ~0.8% annualized vs. BoE's 0.3% forecast.

bullets.title: USD/JPY threatens critical 154.78 support; DXY coiling at 200-day MA with neutral bias
bullets.body: USD/JPY has traversed the full 155-160 range and formed a developing head-and-shoulders top; a sustained break below 154.78 (April 2025 38.2% Fib) would trigger more aggressive retracement toward 151.85-150.00. DXY is coiling on its 99.15 200-day moving average with neutral bias; EUR/USD retains bullish trend dynamics while above 1.15 support.

bullets.title: Semiconductors #1 sector in MS model refresh; software vs. semis rotation is the dominant trade
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's refreshed data-driven sector model keeps Semiconductors at #1 and moves Banks to #2 from #3. Separately, Hedgeye is long software and out of semis citing Quad2 dynamics; the High Beta Momentum factor (Long Semis, Short Software) is down 77% since June while the GS AI Software vs. Semis basket is up 18% in the last month.

bullets.title: LULU structural demand collapse: Americas comps -12%, China flipped to -2% from +23% CC
bullets.body: Lululemon Q2 revenue decelerated 700bps to -5% with comps falling 800bps to -10%; Americas worsened to -12% and China reversed from +23% CC to -2% amid improving domestic brand competition. Q2 gross margin fell ~360bps ex-refund and Q3 operating margin is guided at 6.5% vs. 17.0% last year, reflecting severe fixed-cost deleverage.

bullets.title: AVGO AI revenue to double in FY27 then double again FY28; AWS could hit 50%+ growth in some quarters
bullets.body: JPM Tech Sketch highlights AVGO guiding AI revenue to double in FY27 and double again in FY28, while NVDA guided +70% YoY FY28 revenue growth despite continued supply constraints. JPM also flags Amazon AWS Street estimates at +34% YoY for FY27 as too low, with some quarters potentially hitting 50%+ growth.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples recovering: All-SaaS at 5.9x FY+2 EV/Sales, security at 8.6x; IGV +3.6% YTD vs S&P +13.4%
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index trades at 5.9x FY+2 EV/Sales with multiples up 3.98% week-over-week; security at 8.6x (+5.35% WoW). IGV has returned only +3.6% YTD vs. S&P 500's +13.4%, but the a16z thesis gaining traction — AI may disrupt UI but strengthens underlying data/workflows of incumbent systems of record (CRM, DOCU, TEAM).

bullets.title: China EV brands accelerating globally while US legacy EV demand implodes
bullets.body: BYD August NEV sales hit 440k (+17.8% YoY) with overseas shipments surging 134% YoY to a record 189.5k; Zeekr +110% YoY and Xiaomi SU7 surpassed 500k cumulative deliveries. In contrast, US legacy EVs are in freefall: Ford F-150 Lightning down 95.4%, Mach-E down 72.5%, and Ioniq 5 down 51% YoY in August.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO imminent; $45B 2026 revenue assumed at 2GW / 60% utilization, $200B+ at scale
bullets.body: Anthropic's S-1 filing is described as imminent with an expected record-breaking valuation; current model assumes $45B revenue in 2026 at 2GW capacity and $1.75/M token blended price, scaling to $200B+ at 7GW with $1.00/M token prices. Key S-1 risk factors: open-source competition, customer concentration, revenue-per-token compression, and training cost trajectory.
